On the bridge — quick summary of what telemetry shows so far:
- Frontend nginx clusters in us-west-2 saw a CPU/ephemeral I/O pressure event beginning 09:04.
- Token cache (KV) hit rate dropped sharply; we observed heavy KV eviction and increased cold-loads.
- Tail latencies for generation requests increased, which pushed queues to spin up additional workers causing transient 502s (worker oom + retry storms).
- No sign of network partitioning within the cluster — control plane heartbeats OK.

Mitigation options (pros/cons):
1) Canary cross-region reroute to us-west-1 (recommended initial): 10% of traffic now, monitor 10 min -> 50% -> 100%. Pros: fast relief for latency, lower blast radius. Cons: some clients may see regional pin mismatch.
2) Emergency drain + blue-green in us-west-2: higher risk + longer time (~30-90m).
3) Short-term capacity boost (burst GPUs) in us-west-2 + KV warm-up: quick but may not fix root cause and has cost implications.

Requesting approval to start option #1 immediately. Attaching net-trace and proposed evac plan.

- Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

Subject: Post-incident: US-WEST-2 stabilization and next steps

Carlos / team — final update from our end.
- We completed the staged failover to us-west-1 (10% -> 50% -> 100%) between 09:46 and 10:12 PT on Aug 12.
- Latency and error rates returned to baseline for Solstice traffic; we observed normal KV hit rates after pre-warm completed.
- Root cause (post-mortem in progress): an autoscaling regression in the us-west-2 scheduler combined with a spiky cold-start pattern that caused an eviction cascade in the token cache. The scheduler patch is ready; SRE will deploy a hotfix at 04:00 PT tonight.

Next steps / asks:
- We'll share a concise post-mortem (target: Aug 13 EOD).
- Ben will follow up on the one-time credit proposal for impacted customer windows.
- Recommend a joint post-incident customer briefing tomorrow at 10:00 PT — please confirm.

Attachments: incident timeline CSV, proposed credit worksheet (sent to Ben).

Thanks for the quick coordination and patience — reach out if anything regresses.
